Arbeo of Freising: Early Medieval Author and Bishop of Freising

Arbeo of Freising (born unknown, died 783) was a saintly author and the Bishop of Freising from 764 to 783. He is best known for his comprehensive work on the history of the Franks, which covered over 400 pages and included detailed accounts of the lives and reigns of Frankish kings.

This monumental work, titled Historia Francorum, provided a unique insight into the politics, culture, and society of the Franks during the Merovingian period. Its impact extended beyond the realm of history, as it helped shape the development of medieval historiography and influenced later writers such as Einhard and Nithard.

Arbeo's significance extends beyond his historical work, as he played a key role in promoting education and literacy among the clergy during the Carolingian Renaissance. His legacy continues to inspire historians and scholars today, offering valuable insights into the complexities of medieval society and politics.
